items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: This type of average is called a weighted average or weighted mean.

items.label: section_header
items.text: COUNTING THE NUMBER OF ELECTRONS IN AN ATOM

items.label: section_header
items.text: HINT

items.label: text
items.text: Remember that the number of protons is the same as the atomic number of the element.

items.label: text
items.text: Relative atomic mass is the average mass of an atom, taking into account the amount of each isotope present in a naturally occurring sample of an element. It is explained in more detail in Chapter 5.

items.label: text
items.text: You can probably see that a naturally occurring sample of chlorine must contain more of the 35Cl isotope than the 37Cl isotope. This is because the relative atomic mass is closer to 35 than to 37.

items.label: text
items.text: We can calculate the relative atomic mass of an element by knowing how much of each isotope is present in a sample (the isotopic abundances) of that element, and then working out the average mass of an atom. This is done in exactly the same way as you would calculate a weighted average in maths. It can be understood more easily by looking at a worked example.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXAMPLE1

items.label: text
items.text: A naturally occurring sample of the element boron contains 20% 1ºB and 80% 11B. Calculate the relative atomic mass.

items.label: text
items.text: If we imagine there are 100 atoms we can work out that 20% of them, that is 20, will have mass 10 and 80 will have mass 11.

items.label: text
items.text: The total mass of the 20 atoms with mass 10 is 20 × 10.

items.label: text
items.text: The total mass of the 80 atoms with mass 11 is 80 × 11.

items.label: text
items.text: The total mass of all the atoms in the sample is 20 × 10 + 80 × 11.

items.label: text
items.text: There are 100 atoms so we can work out the average by dividing the total mass by the total number of atoms (100):

items.label: formula
items.text: \text {relative atomic mass} = \frac { 2 0 \times 1 0 + 8 0 \times 1 1 } { 1 0 0 } = 1 0 . 8

items.label: text
items.text: Therefore, the relative atomic mass of boron is 10.8.

items.label: text
items.text: Even if there are three or four different isotopes, you still do the calculation in the same way: calculate the total mass of 100 atoms, then divide the answer by 100.

items.label: section_header
items.text: THE ELECTRONS

items.label: text
items.text: Ato  l (t t   T t   on a proton (+1) is equal but opposite to the charge on an electron (-1), and therefore in an atom:

items.label: text
items.text: number of electrons = number ofprotons

items.label: text
items.text: So, if an oxygen atom (atomic number = 8) has 8 protons, it must also have 8 electrons; if a chlorine atom (atomic number = 17) has 17 protons, it must also have 17 electrons.

items.label: text
items.text: You will see that the key feature in this is knowing the atomic number. You can find the atomic number from the Periodic Table.

items.label: text
items.text: The number of protons in an atom is equal to the number of electrons. However, the atomic number is defined in terms of the number of protons because the number of electrons can change in chemical reactions, for example when atoms form ions (see Chapter 7).
